cohort: 1,098,268 Japanese women with a singleton delivery and no congenital anomaly at 22 weeks or later between 2007 and 2015
finding: Women carrying a male fetus had higher risks of placental abruption, preterm delivery, instrumental delivery, and cesarean delivery, but lower risks of preeclampsia, placenta accreta, atonic hemorrhage, and maternal blood transfusion.
mod_finding: Women carrying a male fetus had a higher risk of cesarean delivery compared to those carrying a female fetus.
